story: When his father gave away old, useless cows at a sacrifice, young Nachiketa kept asking 'To whom will you give me?' until his father snapped, 'To Death!' Nachiketa went to Yama's house, waited three days without food, and was granted three boons. He refused every kind of wealth and asked what happens after death.
belief: The Katha Upanishad records Yama's teaching to him about the undying self. He is the model of the sincere seeker.
turns: His persistence angered his father and sent him to Death's door, but it also earned him the greatest teaching.
facts: Yama's lesson to him, choosing shreyas (the good) over preyas (the pleasant), is one of the Upanishads' best-known teachings.
Swami Vivekananda said that with ten or twelve young people with Nachiketa's faith, he could change the country.
Yama tested him by offering kingdoms, a long life and celestial companions.
